title: Centre Blocks Telangana CM Revanth Reddy's U.S. Visit by Denying Political Clearance
excerpt: Despite court permission to travel, the BJP-led central government has refused MEA clearance for the Congress chief minister's multi-country investment tour, deepening Centre-state tensions.
body:
• The Indian central government has denied political clearance for Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy's planned visit to the United States, effectively cancelling a multi-country investment tour despite court permission to travel.
  • A Hyderabad court had on August 3 allowed Reddy — accused in a 2015 cash-for-vote case — to travel to the U.K., U.S., Germany, and China from August 17 to September 10, subject to MEA political clearance.
  • The denial follows a pattern of Centre-state friction over foreign travel clearances for opposition-ruled state leaders, similar to Karnataka IT Minister Priyank Kharge's blocked U.S. trip in 2025.
  • Reddy's previous U.S. tours secured over Rs 31,500 crore in investment commitments for Telangana, making the blocked visit a setback for the state's economic diplomacy.

Court Said Yes, Centre Said No

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy's planned visit to the United States has been cancelled after the central government denied political clearance through the Ministry of External Affairs, according to WION and The Hindu.

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2090764736451457129

The decision comes despite a Hyderabad court order on August 3 that explicitly permitted Reddy to travel abroad. The Principal Special Judge for SPE and ACB Cases had allowed the Chief Minister to visit the United Kingdom, the United States, Germany, and China from August 17 to September 10, releasing his surrendered passport under specific bail conditions.

But the court's permission came with a critical caveat: Reddy needed political clearance from the MEA, the standard protocol for chief ministers traveling abroad. The BJP-led central government's decision not to grant that clearance has effectively grounded the Congress chief minister.

Why Reddy's Passport Is Under Court Control

Reddy's passport has been held by the courts since 2015, when he was arrested as a Telugu Desam Party (TDP) MLA in a cash-for-vote scandal. He was accused of paying Rs 50 lakh to Elvis Stephenson, a nominated MLA, to secure support for a TDP nominee in the 2015 Telangana Legislative Council elections.

After spending nearly a month in jail, Reddy and co-accused were granted bail by the Telangana High Court, which directed him to surrender his passport and apply to the ACB court before any foreign travel. A chargesheet was filed under the Prevention of Corruption Act and Section 120B (criminal conspiracy) of the Indian Penal Code. Reddy's petition to quash the case remains pending in the Supreme Court.

Despite the pending case, Reddy — who switched from TDP to Congress and became Telangana's Chief Minister in December 2023 — has made several successful foreign trips, including to the World Economic Forum in Davos and an investment-focused U.S. tour in August 2024 that yielded over Rs 31,500 crore in commitments, according to the Telangana CMO.

A Pattern of Blocked Travel

The denial fits a pattern that opposition parties have criticized as politically motivated. In June 2025, Karnataka's IT Minister Priyank Kharge — also from the Congress party — saw his U.S. trip clearance initially blocked by the MEA before the decision was reversed after media attention, according to Devdiscourse.

Kharge publicly criticized the MEA, questioning why the clearance denial was reversed only after the issue gained traction in the press. He accused the Centre of creating contradictions between India's strategic positioning and the bureaucratic obstacles placed before state leaders seeking international collaborations.

"It is for the Indian Government to immediately set up a mechanism to resolve this amicably keeping the interests of our tech population and skilled workers."

— A. Revanth Reddy, Telangana Chief Minister, on U.S.-India relations

Stakes for Telangana's Economy

The blocked visit is a tangible setback for Telangana's investment promotion strategy. Reddy's previous U.S. tour included roundtable conferences on AI and semiconductors, meetings with CEOs from Apple, Google, Amazon, and PepsiCo, and the announcement of a Charles Schwab Global Capability Center in Hyderabad, according to the Telangana CMO's statements on X.

Hyderabad hosts close to 200 U.S. companies and has positioned itself as a leading destination for Global Capability Centers across AI, cloud computing, and life sciences. The Chief Minister's office had planned the current tour to build on that momentum with visits to the U.K., U.S., Germany, and China.

Diaspora Implications

Reddy has been a vocal advocate for the Telugu diaspora in the U.S., recently pressing U.S. Ambassador Jennifer Gor for faster H-1B visa processing and expanded consular services during her visit to Hyderabad. The blocked trip means planned meetings with Telugu NRI communities and tech professionals in American cities will not take place.

What's Next

Reddy's legal team could challenge the clearance denial, though the MEA's political clearance process for state leaders traveling abroad lacks a formal appeals mechanism. The Telangana CMO has not issued an official statement on the cancellation. With the court-permitted travel window extending to September 10, there remains a narrow possibility the clearance could be reconsidered — but the precedent from similar cases suggests the Centre is unlikely to reverse course without significant political pressure.
